components.gap: Item 3's owed existence claim ('Such a choice exists, including the possible zero-risk singular case') is not proved with written steps. Annex lines 313-321 restate a general bracketing fact ('the upper-tail mass brackets every prescribed value between its strict and weak tails at an appropriate quantile') and support it only by 'This follows directly from the inverse-CDF construction in the preceding proof, or from the same continuity argument as thm:p15-likelihood-threshold' -- a deferral in place of the derivation. That lemma is stated and proved for P_0 and a P_0-a.s. finite likelihood ratio, not for the mixture M=L_0Q_0^{n}+L_1Q_1^{n}, under which T_n can carry an infinite atom. components.gap: Hypotheses are incomplete (failure condition 'unstated assumption'): the entry never states its observation space, yet the exact identity sup_{R in H_1} E_R N_{a,b} = E_{Q_1} N_{a,b} = (1-(3/5)^r)/(2/5) and its annex derivation (lines 487-514: 'its mass p at one ranges over [2/5,3/5]', 'Every term is nonincreasing in p, so the worst expectation over the full alternative class occurs at p=2/5') hold only if every contamination H is supported on {0,1}. The chapter's own setting allows an arbitrary measurable space with H any probability (def lines 14-18), and the score convention r=1 on the common null set (robust-hypothesis-testing.tex 81-84), with the nominal densities taken as zero off {0,1}, gives every point outside {0,1} the score b*max(c',1)=4/5. Example: on X={0,1,2} with H=delta_2 and a=3c, E_R N is about 2.168, which exceeds E_{Q_1}N=49/25. So the stated supremum is supplied only under the unstated restriction X={0,1}. The remaining assertions (null computation, error values, limits 5/2 and 2, fixed-b error decay) are written.

defect_observations.note: k_+ existence/uniqueness in annex:p15.huber.tv.pair discharged by 'has the analogous property' (C005 gap).
Identification of the transfer regions {k_-s>p_1}, {p_1>k_+s} with {r<c'}, {r>c''} is asserted via the source's eq. (6), not derived (C005 secondary gap).

Equalizer-threshold existence deferred to 'follows directly from the inverse-CDF construction ... or the same continuity argument as thm:p15-likelihood-threshold', a lemma stated for P_0 and a P_0-a.s. finite ratio rather than the mixture M with a possible infinite atom (C008 gap).

Observation space of the singular example unstated; the exact worst-case expected-size identity fails if contaminants may charge points outside {0,1} (computed: X={0,1,2}, H=delta_2, a=3c gives about 2.168 > 49/25) (C012 gap).
Notation clash: 'Write l,u for the lower and upper score endpoints' reuses u, which in the adjacent contamination-pair proof is the normalization solution c'=u (there the upper endpoint is b/v).

Monotonicity of the extended endpoint ratio on S at one-sided support points (values 0 and infinity) is asserted ('implies') without the short zero-density case check; it is elementary and is not counted as a gap.
One-sided support cases of q_1/q_0 handled by 'The same calculation ... covers' with only the v>0, p_0=0<p_1 case computed. Accepted as direct substitution into the displayed density formulas.

Alternative half of thm:p15-robust-sequential-asymptotic given by mirror ('in the same proof', 'the same calculation', 'identical reasoning'). Accepted because each mirrored premise (E_{R_1}e^{-gamma}<=1, lower exit<=e^A, E_{R_1}gamma>=kappa_1) and resulting bound is written; a stricter reading would make this partial too.

Clause 'infinite entropy can also occur with equivalent laws and finite scores everywhere' is neither proved in annex:p15.directional.log.integrability nor cross-referenced; it is established only by thm:p15-infinite-entropy-finite-scores (lines 288-316).

'Equality of two infinite means does not imply that conclusion' is neither proved in annex:p15.robust.endpoint.closure nor cross-referenced; it is established by thm:p15-singular-contamination-stopping (lines 337-340, annex 523-526).

The chapter's inline locators cite Secs. 2-4, 7 (line 9) and Sec. 8 (line 419) only. Content attributed to 'the source' from Huber Sec. 5 (thm:p15-robust-sequential-errors, -asymptotic; printed pp. 1756-1757) and Sec. 6 (thm:p15-robust-mlr-extension; p. 1757) has no locator in this chapter, and Sec. 6 has none in either chapter. Checked against the held PDF: the attributions are supported.

The source's problem (ii) (printed p. 1754) constrains the loss-weighted size sup R(Q_0',phi)=L_0*A<=alpha; the handbook's level problem uses A<=alpha. Equivalent after rescaling alpha, but the loss-scaled source form is not recorded.

The source's proof (printed p. 1757) concludes eventual pointwise domination E_{Q_0}N>=E_{Q_0'}N for large |K'|. The handbook formalizes 'asymptotically least favorable' as the worst-case ratio limit. Its per-law formulas yield the domination form for finite unequal means, but that form is not stated and is not addressed in the infinite-mean regimes. 'Close the unbounded-score endpoint' holds under the ratio reading.
